IBEW.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Indoor Locals — Friday, August 7, 2026**

**LU-481 Indianapolis, IN** is running *hot* — three mega data center jobs stacked and paying serious overscale. Meade Electric on Meta Lebanon is **$53.80/hr** (10% above scale) running 5-12s Mon-Fri plus Saturday; Ermco's Google Mooresville gig is new construction 5-10s with weekend Saturdays; Eli Lilly work splits between two shops doing 6-10s on new build K153 and 196 Southside. Book depth sits around 144 hands against 31 calls — Book 1 moving fast.

**LU-494 Milwaukee, WI** has three contractors all chasing the Port Washington Data Center at **JW wage plus $10/hr premium** — Cupertino, MJ Electric, and Gurtz all competing for the same 30-18-15 hand slots. Hours vary (50-58 to 60 per week depending on contractor), but the addon is real money. 38 calls against 199 hands keeps pressure low; this is grab-and-go work if you clear the drug screen.

**LU-430 Racine, WI** owns the Microsoft Mount Pleasant build at **$62.51/hr flat** — Gerdes, Pieper, Staff, and Kelso-Burnett all hiring. WI Inside card or 2+ years reciprocal required; long sleeves mandatory. 11 calls, 76 hands deep; this one's not starving but solid and local.

**LU-291 Boise, ID** is the per diem goldmine: Micron ID1 jobs are **$45.33/hr scale + $170/day per diem** (7 days if eligible) on a PLA gig. Prime Controls leading with 48 Inside JW slots; Quality and VECA splitting remainder. 60/60/50 rotating schedules on the big push.

**LU-613 Atlanta, GA** keeps grinding — 65 calls, 357 hands, **$40–$40.90/hr** on hospital and data center cable work. Inglett & Stubbs and Whitehead Electric are steady, not flashy.

The money's chasing data centers and institutional build-outs in the Midwest and Mountain West — per diem is king when scale is capped, and the 5-10s/6-10s grind is becoming standard on these mega-projects.

LINEMAN.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Lineman Locals — Friday, August 7, 2026**

**LU-291 Boise, ID** is running hot on the Micron ID1 build-out. Prime Controls and Quality Electric are pulling **48 and 7 journeymen** respectively at **$45.33/hr** plus **$170/day per diem** (7 days if eligible) on a brutal 60/60/50 schedule—that's inside wirework but the money stacks fast. Quality's also got 5 hands on the St. Luke's Tower job at **$55.33/hr**, straight 5-8s if you need breathing room. PLA gig means background and drug screen locked in.

**LU-1426 Grand Forks, ND** has Parsons Electric cranking through the Polaris Forge Data Center with **92 inside journeymen** (two separate calls, 48 and 44 each) at **$44.80/hr** plus **$100/day non-taxed per diem**, weekday incentives, and **$150 Saturdays/Sundays**. 6-10s grind, 100+ mile radius, but the incentive bump makes it worth the haul from out west.

**LU-71 Columbus, OH** has New River Electric Corp running **40 journeymen** on distribution work at top scale (unlisted but typically strong) with **$125/night stayed, $125 bonus on 10-hour days**, CDL A, 6-10s. Another crew of 9 in Southern Ohio, 4-10s with optional weekends. Capital Electric's got 6 hands on cable splicing in Johnstown at **$100/day per diem**.

**LU-1547 Anchorage, AK** is lean at **63 hands across 48 calls**—mostly non-union scale work (laborers, tree trimmers at $43.55), but Alaska rates typically run high. Chugach Electric's hiring member service reps, not linework.

**LU-175 Chattanooga, TN** has **78 hands** spread across data-center and nuclear TVA work—Adman Electric's pulling 25 on the DNN4 build, Lawson's hiring 12 on day shift in Dalton. Rotating shifts, nuclear clearance required on the Watts Bar calls.

Data centers and transmission builds are absorbing the board—this market's riding infrastructure and private-sector power play, not storm response.

UA.text:
**Trampin the UA Locals — Friday, August 7, 2026**

**LU-140 Salt Lake City, UT** is running hot with 18 calls eating 61 hands. BCS Mechanical's got the volume play here—15 JW pipefitters and 13 JW plumbers on the Sego Project in West Valley, all locked into 4-10s starting August 3rd with OT kicking in. DSI's also hunting 6 JW pipefitters for QTS in Eagle Mountain on a 5-8 grind that stretches to 5-10s some weeks. This is the board to chase if you want sustained hours and stack work quick.

**LU-290 Portland, OR** shows 21 calls on 30 hands—tight ratio. Charter Mechanical's running 4 orbital welders at Intel Ronler Acres in Hillsboro (Ticket #71459), specialty tool install work. PermaCold's got 3 commercial refrig tech slots in the metro. If you've got BIM skills or are a solid orbital guy, Portland's moving product.

**LU-208 Denver, CO** isn't massive—13 calls, 28 hands—but the specs matter. US Eng. Metalworks wants high-purity tube-bending fitters and stainless TIG welders for Broadcom in Fort Collins. Apollo's pushing 6/10 days at DC2 Data Center in Aurora on commercial rate plus incentive. Corden Pharma in Boulder's running combo welders nights, 5/10s, with a $125 per diem if you're 100+ miles out.

**LU-213 & LU-325 St. John and Fredericton, NB** are both locked on Irving Oil Refinery and Irving Pulp & Paper—solid 4-10 day-shift work under GPMA/Industrial Ag agreements. Not flashy but stable.

**LU-192 Cheyenne, WY** has the outlier: PMI's pushing fitters, welders, and plumbers to Ellsworth AFB in South Dakota with a $100/day per diem. OSHA 10 required.

Semiconductor, data center, and refinery outage work is pulling hands hard—specialized skills are moving fastest.
